note: F-034: SLH-DSA-SHA2-256f must use FORS tree height a=9 (FIPS 205 Table 2: n=32, h=68, d=17, h'=4, a=9, k=35, lg_w=4, m=49, 49,856-byte signature); every tier shipped a=8 (48,736-byte signature, 44-byte digest). The pubkey and signatures below were NOT produced by this repo: they come from the third-party PyPI package slh-dsa 0.2.5 (github.com/colinxu2020/slhdsa), class Sha2_1Parameter(25, 32, 68, 17, 4, 9, 35, 4, 49) -- that library's FIPS 205 Sec 11.2.1 SHA-256-only instantiation (the repo's on-chain variant, since Bitcoin Script has no OP_SHA512, issue #137) at the 256f dimensions. Internal (pre-hash-free) slh_sign_internal, deterministic (opt_rand = PK.seed), seeds sk_seed/sk_prf/pk_seed = SHA-256('runar F-034 sk_seed' / 'runar F-034 sk_prf' / 'runar F-034 pk_seed'), msg = UTF-8 'runar F-034 SLH-DSA-SHA2-256f a=9 witness'. Before the fix the compiled verifier REJECTED this honest signature (its OP_SIZE gate demanded 48,736 bytes); with only a corrected it still aborted at `8 OP_NUM2BIN`, because this signature's 64-bit tree index 0x9cc4feac04b4276d is >= 2^63 (true for about half of all 256f signatures, independent of a). The fold-ON compile of the fixture source runs on @bsv/sdk Spend.

spends.note: honest a=9 signature from the independent slh-dsa 0.2.5 signer -- rejected by the pre-fix a=8 verifier

the same signature with the low bit of its final byte (the top XMSS authentication-path node of hypertree layer 16) flipped -- the correct length, so it passes the OP_SIZE gate and must be rejected by the hypertree root comparison

goldenHashesNote: F-034 moved this golden (old sha256 7bc507fc630384e99830c12c969de166f403d3ef955d781dd6c68c8e38ec83ed, previously justified by a route-B allowlist entry that is now removed). Two defects, both in the SHA2_256f verifier and both rejecting honest signatures: (1) FORS tree height a=8 instead of FIPS 205 Table 2's a=9 in all 7 tiers (OP_SIZE gate 48,736 instead of 49,856 bytes; 44-byte instead of 49-byte digest); (2) the first tree address was encoded with `8 OP_NUM2BIN`, but 256f's tree index has h - h' = 64 bits and is >= 2^63 for about half of all signatures, whose minimal script number needs a 9th sign byte, so the script aborted (now `9 OP_NUM2BIN 8 OP_SPLIT OP_DROP`; only 256f has h - h' >= 64, no other golden moves). Both were reproduced by EXECUTION before the fix, against signatures this repo did not produce (slh-dsa 0.2.5, Sha2_1Parameter at the 256f dimensions; at a=8 that library's signature is byte-identical to this repo's TS reference signer, so it is the same SHA-256-only scheme): the old golden rejected the a=9 signature at its OP_SIZE gate and the library's a=8 signature (tree index 0x944e93da779cc4fe >= 2^63) at OP_NUM2BIN. The new golden BYTES (fold-OFF) were executed directly on the @bsv/sdk interpreter with this spec's pubkey spliced in: honest a=9 signature accepted (592,788 ops), the tampered spend rejected only after the full run (final root comparison), the a=8 signature rejected at the OP_SIZE gate. The spends above re-execute the fold-ON compile on Spend. All seven compilers emit these bytes (conformance golden 85/85; multi-format 9/9 surfaces in both fold modes). The pin is deliberately self-invalidating: any later change to expected-script.hex must come back through this witness.
